name: ImagiKnit (San Francisco)
description: A deep, colourful yarn shop on 18th Street with its own class programme, a good first stop for fibre and a gentle way to meet the city's knitters.
details: Runs classes at both its San Francisco and Berkeley shops (separate class calendars on the site). Stocks local yarns alongside kits, needles and books.

image.alt: A hand-dyed skein held up in front of shelves of yarn at ImagiKnit

name: Atelier Yarns (Divisadero)
description: Yarn shop that lists weaving classes and weaving tools alongside knitting and crochet, so a likely place to find loom-curious company in the city.
details: Class menu on the site covers knitting and crochet instruction, special techniques and weaving classes; carries locally made and hard-to-find yarns. Sister shop in San Rafael.

image.alt: A pink hand-knitted shawl made with Atelier Yarns

name: Britex Fabrics
description: San Francisco's grand old fabric house near Union Square, worth visiting just for the walls of buttons, laces and hand-dyed silk ribbons.
details: Brick-and-mortar store with fabrics (silks, wools, brocades, linens), buttons in horn, bone, shell and corozo, vintage and heirloom lace trims, and a personal swatch-shopper service.

image.alt: Embossed brocade fabric in folds, from Britex Fabrics

name: Mendel's (Haight Street)
description: Long-running independent art and craft supply store in the Haight, the kind of shop where you go in for one thing and leave with a new project.
details: Many but not all in-store products are on the website; the shop invites you to ask for hard-to-find items.

name: SCRAP (creative reuse depot)
description: Ruth Asawa's gift to the city: a creative-reuse depot where donated fabric, paper and odd materials are sold cheaply to artists and teachers.
details: Runs a materials depot, a workshop calendar and a Sustainable Fashion Design programme. Material drop-offs Tue-Sat 10am-3pm (per the site).

image.alt: Cubbies of colourful fabric scraps under the SCRAP sign at SCRAP in San Francisco

name: San Francisco Quilters Guild
address: St. Anne of the Sunset, San Francisco
description: The city's quilting guild, meeting in person at St. Anne of the Sunset, with monthly lectures, workshops and community quilt-making.
details: Upcoming: talk 'From fast fashion to sustainable stitching' with Radha Weaver (Nov 10); QUILT SF 2027 show April 2-3, 2027. Also runs Lincoln Park Quilters and a block of the month.

image.alt: Two guild members sitting with finished quilts across their laps

name: Loom and Shuttle Guild
address: 501 Laguna Honda Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94127
description: San Francisco's weaving guild since 1948, around 60 weavers of every level working on all kinds of looms, and open to visitors.
details: Meets 10am at St. John's United Church of Christ, 501 Laguna Honda Blvd (first Saturday of even months per the CNCH guild list at cnch.org/guilds; odd months at members' homes). The guild's own online programme calendar was last updated for 2021-22, so confirm dates by email before going.

image.alt: A hand-woven blue scarf with fringe

name: Textile Arts Council (Fine Arts Museums of SF)
address: 50 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA 94118
description: Support group for the textile department of the Fine Arts Museums, with lectures, tours and workshops: the best single door into the city's textile scholars and collectors.
details: Runs an Ethnic Textiles Study Group, a Bay Area Fiber Artists Archive, public lecture recordings and an annual Textile Bazaar (2026: Nov 7, 10am-4pm, St Mary's Cathedral Event Center, 1111 Gough St). Mapped at the de Young.

image.alt: A purple tie-dyed shawl with beaded tassels

name: Textile Arts Council Textile Bazaar 2026
description: One-day bazaar of textile artists, makers and dealers in global and vintage textiles: a place to look, buy and maybe one day show her own weaving.
details: Saturday Nov 7, 2026, 10am-4pm at St Mary's Cathedral Event Center, 1111 Gough St at Geary. All vendor spaces for 2026 are filled; watch for the next call.

image.alt: Hands holding a strand of beadwork, black and white photograph

name: San Francisco Public Library craft workshops
description: Free, drop-in craft workshops around the branch libraries, such as sashiko embroidery sessions in May 2026: an easy, no-cost way to meet neighbourhood makers.
details: Programs are drop-in with no registration unless noted. Check sfpl.org events for the current craft calendar; locations rotate between branches, so this pin is approximate.

image.alt: The San Francisco Main Library seen from Civic Center

name: Lacis Museum of Lace and Textiles
description: A free lace and textile museum joined to a textile-arts emporium and class programme, where she can study bobbin lace one hour and learn beaded embroidery the next.
details: Free tours Monday-Saturday; classes from embroidery basics to Victorian garment construction and lace-making (e.g. Beaded Cabochon, Nov 14, 2026, $55). Current exhibits include Normandy Lace. New East Bay Lacers group.

image.alt: A panel of antique lace with embroidered flowers from the Lacis Museum collection
image.credit: Image: Lacis Museum of Lace and Textiles

name: ImagiKnit (Berkeley)
description: ImagiKnit's Elmwood shop, with its own class calendar for knitters and crocheters on the Berkeley side of the bay.
details: Classes in Berkeley are listed separately from San Francisco on the shop's site.

image.alt: Hands knitting a ribbed orange piece beside a ball of chunky yarn

name: A Verb for Keeping Warm
description: Oakland yarn and fabric shop built around natural dye, selling mordants, dyes and dyeables and teaching classes: the closest thing to a natural-dye home base in the East Bay.
details: In-store shopping Fridays and Saturdays 11am-3pm; curbside pickup Tue-Fri. Carries its own AVFKW yarns and fabric, mending and embroidery supplies, basket-making materials and a class and trunk-show calendar.

image.alt: Wall-to-wall shelves of yarn inside Verb for Keeping Warm

name: Stonemountain & Daughter Fabrics
description: Big Berkeley fabric store with deep linen, Japanese and Indian-import shelves and its own sewing classes.
details: Stocks double gauze, ikats and Indian imports, Japanese imports, linen, silks, wools and designer deadstock; site links to sewing classes.

image.alt: The pink storefront of Stonemountain and Daughter Fabrics in Berkeley

name: East Bay Depot for Creative Reuse
description: Oakland's sustainable art and craft supply store, stocked with donated materials at low prices: good hunting for yarn, fabric and odd things to weave with.
details: Store and donation centre on Telegraph Avenue; phone 510-547-6470 per the site footer.

name: Bay Quilts
description: Richmond fabric store and quilt gallery with a deep stock of solids and quilting cottons.
details: Kona solids, Tula Pink collections, threads and batting. Hello Stitch Studio (closing end of 2026) has held classes here.

name: Golden Gate Weavers
description: East Bay weaving guild, active in 2026 with monthly meetings, newsletters and a joint exhibition with the Bay Area Basket Makers.
details: Meets 3rd Mondays at 9:30am at Sports Basement, 2727 Milvia St (per the CNCH guild list). Monthly newsletters posted through October 2026. Spring 2026 show 'Tradition, Innovation, and Back' with BABM at Richmond Art Center.

image.alt: A striped textile in progress on a loom

name: Spindles & Flyers Spinning Guild
description: Berkeley spinning guild whose members also weave, dye, felt, sprang and make baskets, and who welcome newcomers to monthly meetings.
details: Meets usually the fourth Sunday, September-June (Finnish Hall, 1970 Chestnut St per CNCH). Next: Nov 22, 2026, 11am, 'Ergonomics for Makers' with Andrea Lui (Zoom only).

image.alt: A member holding a notebook of handspun fibre and knitted samples

name: Bay Area Basket Makers
description: Guild of Bay Area basketmakers working in fibre, gourds, kelp, wire and felt, active in 2026 with meetings, workshops and a Richmond Art Center exhibition.
details: Meets first Saturday, 10:30am (Chatham School, Oakland, per the CNCH list). 2026 posts include workshops with Vicki Assegued and the joint exhibition with Golden Gate Weavers; resource list names The Caning Shop in Berkeley. Pin is approximate.

image.alt: A blue coiled basket with cut-out waves

name: East Bay Heritage Quilters
description: Large East Bay quilt guild with lectures, workshops, weekly open quilting and even a 2026 Japan textile tour.
details: Wednesday Open Quilting at Albany United Methodist Church community room, 980 Stannage Ave (e.g. Oct 28, 2026, 9am). Community Quilts programme and an ACAC 2026-2027 exhibit call.

image.alt: A quilt with an orange moon over a patchwork city skyline

name: Treadles to Threads Spinners Guild
description: Friendly Contra Costa spinning guild that welcomes beginners and lends out equipment, so she can try a wheel before buying one.
details: Meets at Pleasant Hill Senior Center, 233 Gregory Lane (e.g. Sept 23, 2026, 7-9pm; last Wednesday Jan-Nov per CNCH). Runs dye days, a Fiber Frolic and eco-printing programmes.

image.alt: A striped handwoven textile on a loom

name: Conference of Northern California Handweavers (CNCH)
address: 2660 Ygnacio Valley Rd, Walnut Creek, CA 94598
description: The umbrella for Northern California's weaving and spinning guilds, running a conference with multi-day classes: the 2027 edition is in Redwood City.
details: 2026 conference at Asilomar offered tablet weaving, inkle, rigid heddle, shibori, painted warps and pine-needle basket classes. Publishes the regional guild list with meeting places, plus a conference grant. Mapped at the Walnut Creek address listed on its site.

image.alt: Skeins of hand-dyed yarn hanging in a row

name: Atelier Yarns (San Rafael)
description: Atelier's Marin shop, with the same mix of yarn, weaving tools and classes as the Divisadero store.
details: See the Atelier site for class schedules at each location.

image.alt: A knitted cap and cowl in cream wool made with Atelier Yarns

name: Dharma Trading Co.
address: 1604 Fourth St, San Rafael, CA 94901 (per OpenStreetMap)
description: Dye supplier for natural dyes, extracts and mordants, silk-painting and tie-dye supplies, and undyed cotton, silk and wool to dye.
details: Online catalogue covers natural dyeing, batik, marbling, tub dyeing and screen printing, with phone craft support (800-542-5227). Store location taken from OpenStreetMap; confirm hours before visiting.

image.alt: A tie-dyed fabric with a kaleidoscope pattern

name: Fibershed Learning Center
address: 14000 Point Reyes-Petaluma Rd, Point Reyes Station, CA 94956
description: The Marin non-profit behind the 'fibershed' idea of locally grown, dyed and sewn clothing, with workshops and markets at its Learning Center on Black Mountain Ranch.
details: Learning Center open only for scheduled events and workshops (e.g. Broom-making with Abeni Pierson, Oct 10, 2026); inquiries to learningcenter@fibershed.org. Runs symposia, a producer directory, the Weaving Voices podcast and seasonal markets.

image.alt: A woman arranging yellow-green plant material on a table at an outdoor Fibershed event

name: Bolinas Museum
description: Small free museum of coastal Marin art and history; its winter show 'Paul Harris: The Boy Sews Like An Angel' runs Oct 31, 2026-Jan 3, 2027.
details: Open Friday 1-5pm and Saturday-Sunday 12-5pm; admission always free.

image.alt: The white clapboard buildings of the Bolinas Museum

name: Black Sheep Handweavers Guild
description: Peninsula weaving guild (HGA and CNCH affiliated) whose evening meetings mix members' show-and-tell with an outside speaker.
details: Meets 3rd Thursdays, 7:15pm (social 6:45pm) at Veterans' Memorial Senior Center, 1455 Madison Ave (per the CNCH guild list).

image.alt: A small handwoven piece on a table loom

name: Glenna Harris Weavers Guild
description: San Jose weaving and spinning guild with an education programme and public demonstrations; visitors are welcome at monthly meetings.
details: Meets the second Monday of each month, mostly at the Sobrato Community Conference Center, 1400 Parkmoor Ave (some meetings at members' homes; email first).

image.alt: A pink handwoven piece on a loom with a shuttle

name: San Jose Museum of Quilts & Textiles
description: San Jose museum devoted to quilts and textiles, with rotating exhibitions, a searchable collection, and events and workshops.
details: Site lists exhibitions, events and workshops, a 50th-anniversary programme, SoFA pocket-park murals and 'Fiber Arts for Beginners' resources. Note its web address is now sj-mqt.org.

image.alt: A gallery of quilts at the San Jose Museum of Quilts and Textiles
image.credit: Image: San Jose Museum of Quilts and Textiles

name: Humanmade
description: 13,000-square-foot SoMa makerspace with wood, metal, textiles, electronics and digital-fabrication shops open to members after training.
details: Memberships, equipment training and project workshops; also runs workforce programmes and a hardware accelerator. Open Mon-Fri 9am-9pm, Sat-Sun 10am-6pm.

image.alt: An instructor guiding a student at a milling machine at Humanmade

name: WorkshopSF
description: Haight Street studio of one-evening adult craft classes, from leatherworking and printmaking to textiles and wood, ideal for sampling a new medium.
details: Free First Friday pop-ups (e.g. notebook and bookmark making, Nov 6, 2026). Class categories: Art + Printmaking, Leatherworking, Plants, Textile + Craft, Wood + Clay.

image.alt: The long workbench inside Workshop SF

name: Mission Community Woodshop
address: 20 Clinton Park, San Francisco, CA (per OpenStreetMap)
description: Non-profit, professional-grade woodshop in central San Francisco set up for fine furniture, with bench-rental memberships and classes from introductory to advanced.
details: Full- and part-time memberships include a bench, storage and machine access during shop hours. Upcoming: body-surfing handplane class (11/14) and a Craft Fair on Dec 5. Location from OpenStreetMap; confirm via the site's contact page.

image.alt: Machines and benches in the Mission Community Woodshop

name: Wood Thumb
description: Traditional SoMa woodshop running beginner-friendly public workshops where you build a finished piece in a session, plus private shop time.
details: Public workshops need no experience; also offers team events, shop time and custom woodcut prints.

image.alt: A hand-held drill cutting wood at Wood Thumb

name: Metalworks SF
description: North Beach school of hand-fabricated jewelry in silver, copper and brass, with lost-wax classes and bench rental, linked to Macchiarini Design.
details: Class schedule 2026-2027 posted on the site; also group events and DIY wedding-ring sessions.

image.alt: Two metalsmiths working with a torch at Metalworks SF

name: Metal Arts Guild San Francisco
description: Bay Area metalsmiths' guild since 1951, with lectures and demos, workshops, exhibitions and a member directory of local schools and studios.
details: MAG and Barbara M. Berk scholarship applications open (deadline Oct 31, 2026). Runs Metalsmithing Day and an 'Elevate Our Art' programme. PO Box only, so the pin is approximate.

image.alt: Students and an instructor with a torch at a metalworking bench
image.credit: Image: Metal Arts Guild of San Francisco

name: Public Glass
description: San Francisco's centre for glass art and education, with intro classes, longer courses and rentable hot, flame, fusing and cold shops.
details: Memberships with studio orientation, blowslot rentals, a scholarship programme and 'Hot Glass Cold Beer' events.

image.alt: Two glassblowers shaping a glowing gather of glass at a bench at Public Glass

name: Exploratorium Tinkering Studio
description: The Exploratorium's Tinkering Studio is its workshop for hands-on making and learning; the museum's After Dark Thursdays are a good evening out.
details: Pier 15 (Embarcadero at Green Street). 'Glow' runs Nov 19-Jan 24. Also hosts Arts & Artists and Osher Fellows programmes.

image.alt: Visitors at a smoke-vortex exhibit in the Exploratorium
image.credit: D'Arcy Norman from Calgary, Canada / Wikimedia Commons

name: Building REsources
description: San Francisco's non-profit salvage yard of reusable building and landscaping materials, nearly three-quarters of an acre of wood, tile and found objects.
details: Hosts a Deconstruction Workshop (Apr 17, 2026) and plant exchanges.

image.alt: Racks of salvaged doors in the yard at Building Resources

name: The Crucible
description: Oakland's big industrial-arts school, teaching glass, metal, clay, wood and more since 1999, with studio access, scholarships and free public tours.
details: Events include a Hot Art Halloween iron pour and GIFTY, its holiday craft fair (Dec 5-6, 2026). Adult classes, studio access, private instruction and youth programmes.

image.alt: A student working with a torch at a Crucible bench

name: GIFTY: The Crucible's Holiday Craft Fair
description: Two floors of handmade goods from 60+ Oakland and Bay Area artists at The Crucible, with live demos and kids' activities.
details: December 5-6, 2026: Sat 10am-6pm, Sun 11am-4pm.

image.alt: An instructor working a glowing gather of glass in the hot shop at The Crucible

name: Ace Makerspace
description: Member-run 24/7 makerspace with a textiles area alongside woodshop, metal, laser and CNC tools; 'making is for everyone' is their motto.
details: Suite #214. Tours on the 1st and 3rd Wednesdays and the 2nd and 4th Saturdays (RSVP via the calendar); free guest accounts; course catalogue. Formerly Ace Monster Toys.

image.alt: Members gathered around a work table at ACE Makerspace

name: Hida Tool & Hardware
description: Berkeley shop of authentic Japanese hand tools for woodworking, carving, gardening and the kitchen, a pleasure to visit even before you need a chisel.
details: Also stocks plaster trowels, adzes, bonsai tools and books.

image.alt: A Japanese plane, chisel and hammer laid out on a wooden surface

name: Stained Glass Garden
description: Fourth Street glass shop with classes and studio time in stained glass, mosaic and fusing, plus supplies and custom work.
details: Open 7 days, 10am-5pm; phone 510-841-2200.

name: Maker Nexus
description: South Bay non-profit makerspace with memberships, classes, youth programmes and a Maker Market.
details: Also runs youth programmes and the Tech Challenge; rooms can be booked.

image.alt: A student cutting wood on a table saw at Maker Nexus

name: Bay Area Glass Institute (BAGI)
address: 635 Phelan Ave, San Jose, CA 95122 (per OpenStreetMap)
description: South Bay glass studio offering hands-on glass experiences, studio classes, open-studio rentals and visiting-artist workshops.
details: Visiting artists in 2026 included 'Mixing Glass with Printmaking' (June 17-21, 2026). Location from OpenStreetMap; confirm on the site.

image.alt: A glassblower shaping a piece at the bench in front of an audience at Bay Area Glass Institute

name: Spaulding Marine Center
description: Sausalito waterfront boatworks and maritime centre with adult education (Boatworks 101) and a monthly storytelling series.
details: Visit hours Mon-Fri 7:30am-3:30pm; Woodrum Library on site.

image.alt: Three kids holding wooden toolboxes they built in the Spaulding Marine Center boat shop

name: San Francisco Center for the Book
address: 375 Rhode Island St, San Francisco, CA 94103
description: Thirty years of letterpress and bookbinding in Potrero Hill: weekend workshops, core certificate programmes and a well-equipped print studio.
details: Spring 2027 (Jan-Apr) workshop schedule posts Nov 14, 2026. Exhibition 'The Joyful Body of the Word: Betsy Davids and the Book', Sept 26-Dec 20, 2026.

image.alt: Drawers of wood and metal type at San Francisco Center for the Book
image.credit: Image: San Francisco Center for the Book

name: Crown Point Press
description: Publisher of fine-art etchings since 1962, with a gallery open weekdays and summer workshops in its studio.
details: Enter at 657 Howard St. Current show: Richard Tuttle and Odili Donald Odita, 'Language and Pattern', Aug 17-Nov 30, 2026. Mon-Fri 9am-5pm.

image.alt: The brick building that houses Crown Point Press in San Francisco

name: Arion Press & M&H Type
address: 2 Marina Blvd, Building B, San Francisco, CA 94123
description: Makers of artist books by hand for half a century, with M&H Type and public tours at Fort Mason.
details: Open Tue-Sat 12-5pm (Landmark Building B, Suite 100). Public tours the second Thursday and third Saturday of each month (Fort Mason listing). The Grabhorn Institute runs a King Artist Residency.

image.alt: A fine-press edition of Neruda's Sonetos de Amor, bound in pink cloth and tan leather

name: Graphic Arts Workshop
description: Printmakers' studio in Dogpatch whose members open the space for SF Open Studios.
details: Took part in SF Open Studios in October 2026 with members including Christine Innes, Mark Brodie and Javier Chalini. Location from OpenStreetMap; contact the co-op about membership.

image.alt: The printmaking studio at Graphic Arts Workshop, with a large etching press

name: Kala Art Institute
description: Berkeley print and media-arts centre with artist-in-residence and fellowship programmes, a rentable print room and adult art classes.
details: Residencies include Artist-in-Residence, Fellowship, Veterans, Media Arts, Parent Artist and Print Public programmes; gallery exhibitions and an annual art auction.

image.alt: A student drawing at a worktable in a Kala Art Institute studio

name: CODEX Foundation
description: Berkeley foundation for the handmade book, with a reference library of artists' books, a letterpress studio, lectures and workshops and a biennial international book art fair.
details: Unit D. Library includes the Koch Collection and a consignment collection of artists' books; Emerging Artist Fellowship and research scholarship.

image.alt: Hand-bound artists' books standing open on a table, from the Codex Foundation website

name: Asian Art Museum
description: Civic Center museum of art from across Asia, where Free First Sundays make it easy to return again and again to study surfaces, textiles and form.
details: Hours: Thu 1-8pm, Fri-Mon 10am-5pm, closed Tue-Wed. Calendar of cultural celebrations and talks.

image.alt: The Asian Art Museum in San Francisco's Civic Center

name: Museum of the African Diaspora (MoAD)
description: San Francisco's museum of Black art and culture across the African diaspora, with an Emerging Artist Program and residencies: an important home for a Rwandan maker.
details: Fall 2026 shows include 'Liberatory Living: Protective Interiors & Radical Black Joy' and 'Dewey Crumpler: Sonic Lineages'. Ground floor of the St. Regis; closed Mondays.

image.alt: Paintings hung in a gallery at the Museum of the African Diaspora
image.credit: Image: Museum of the African Diaspora

name: de Young Museum (textile collection)
address: 50 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA 94118
description: The Fine Arts Museums' Golden Gate Park building, home of the textile department that the Textile Arts Council supports with lectures and study groups.
details: Tue-Sun 9:30am-5:15pm (per the TAC site). famsf.org blocks automated checks, so exhibitions were confirmed only through the Textile Arts Council.

image.alt: The de Young Museum in Golden Gate Park

name: SFMOMA
description: San Francisco's museum of modern and contemporary art, a short walk from MoAD and Yerba Buena.
details: Some floors (Atrium, 3-5) are being reinstalled in late 2026; check what is open before visiting.

image.alt: The SFMOMA building in San Francisco

name: California Academy of Sciences
address: 55 Music Concourse Dr, San Francisco, CA 94118
description: Natural history museum, aquarium and planetarium in Golden Gate Park, a place to think about where pigments, fibres and minerals come from; NightLife evenings are adults-only.
details: Across the concourse from the de Young.

image.alt: Sea nettle jellyfish drifting in a tank at the California Academy of Sciences

name: Oakland Museum of California (OMCA)
focusAreas: California art, history and natural science
description: California's art, history and natural sciences under one roof by Lake Merritt, with Friday Nights at OMCA and gallery chats.
details: Programmes: Friday Nights, Spotlight Sundays, Gallery Chats, First Sundays.

image.alt: The Oakland Museum of California building

name: BAMPFA (Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive)
description: UC Berkeley's art museum and cinema, with talks, conversations and hands-on workshops alongside its exhibitions.
details: Open Wed-Sun 11am-7pm. Library and study centres on site.

image.alt: Interior of the Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive

name: UC Botanical Garden at Berkeley
description: A hillside garden of plants from around the world with classes and workshops, a living library for anyone growing or foraging dye and fibre plants.
details: Classes and workshops, adult tours and a plant nursery; 2026 exhibitions include a Maren Hassinger sculpture show.

image.alt: Succulents and aloes in the UC Botanical Garden in Berkeley

name: Cantor Arts Center (Stanford)
description: Stanford's free art museum, currently showing Bay Area Asian American and Chicano art histories in its Archive Room.
details: Shows include 'Archive Room: Irene Poon and Charles Wong' and 'Archive Room: Amalia Mesa-Bains'. Always free.

image.alt: The Cantor Arts Center at Stanford University

name: Museum of the American Indian (Miwok Park)
description: A living cultural centre in Miwok Park on Coast Miwok land, focused on Indigenous lifeways and makers of the Americas rather than static display.
details: Exhibits, events and education programmes; check the site for opening hours.

image.alt: Redwood trunks in woodland, from the Marin Museum of the American Indian website
image.credit: Image: Marin Museum of the American Indian

name: SOMArts Cultural Center
description: Cross-cultural, community-rooted arts centre with printmaking (and ceramics) classes, the Ramp Gallery and the city's best-known Día de los Muertos exhibition.
details: 2026 shows: 'In Their Name: Día de Los Muertos 2026' and the Murphy & Cadogan awards. Currently fundraising to close a $90K gap.

image.alt: A gallery with hanging garments and framed works at SOMArts Cultural Center

name: Root Division
description: Arts non-profit pairing an artist studios programme with adult classes and exhibitions; its December Artist Fair is open to vendors.
details: Artist Fair: Sat Dec 12, 2026, 12-5pm, free, call for vendors open. Also runs Studios Program, fellowships and the Frank-Ratchye Project Space.

image.alt: Framed works and sculptures on display in the Root Division gallery

name: Art Explosion Studios
description: Affordable artist studios in three Mission and Dogpatch buildings, with member open studios and a holiday show.
details: Locations: 2425 17th St, 744 Alabama St and 1661 Tennessee St. Phone 415-323-3020.

name: Hunters Point Shipyard Artists
description: Huge artist studio community in the former naval shipyard (300+ creatives per Hoodline), with 130+ studios opening to the public each spring and fall.
details: Fall 2026 Shipyard Open Studios ran Oct 17-18 (free, RSVP), with satellite studios at Islais Creek; spring 2026 ran Apr 25-26. Organised by the Shipyard Trust for the Arts (shipyardartists.com blocks automated checks).

image.alt: Aerial view of the Hunters Point Naval Shipyard on San Francisco Bay

name: ArtSpan: SF Open Studios
description: San Francisco's citywide open-studios season, now in its 52nd year, when hundreds of artists open their studios neighbourhood by neighbourhood; a route to showing her own work.
details: 2026 tours ran Sept 18-Oct 25 (Hoodline). Run by ArtSpan; artists register through artspan.org. Pin is approximate.

name: Minnesota Street Project
description: Dogpatch cluster of galleries and art spaces in converted warehouses, with a steady rhythm of openings.
details: Fall 2026 shows include 'Character Development' (1201 Minnesota St) and Megan Broughton: False Horizon (1275 Minnesota St). The MSP Foundation supports artists.

image.alt: Paintings hung in a white-walled gallery at Minnesota Street Project

name: Creativity Explored
description: Mission District studio and gallery that has supported artists with disabilities for over 40 years; exhibitions and shop are open to visitors.
details: Youth programmes (Imaginate camps), partner programmes and events and exhibitions.

image.alt: An artist painting at an easel in the Creativity Explored studio

name: Gray Area
description: Art-and-technology centre on Mission Street with courses, workshops, talks and an incubator for artists.
details: Current courses include workshops and webinars (e.g. 11/14/26 on protecting artists online). Creative R&D Labs and free synth and sound workshops.

image.alt: A crowd queuing under the Gray Area marquee at the Grand Theater in San Francisco's Mission District

name: Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture
description: Waterfront arts campus that hosts the big craft fairs (West Coast Craft, Renegade) plus galleries, Arion Press and free exhibitions.
details: Current: Leah Rosenberg, 'The Sea Is But Another Sky'; FOR-SITE at The Guardhouse through Jan 24, 2027.

image.alt: Aerial view of Fort Mason Center on the San Francisco waterfront

name: Long Now Talks
description: A long-running San Francisco lecture series on civilisation-scale ideas, held live on stage and recorded as a podcast.
details: Upcoming: Rick Prelinger, 'Lost Landscapes' (Dec 1), then talks Jan-Apr 2027. Venue varies, so the pin is approximate.

image.alt: The Interval, the bar and library at Fort Mason run by the Long Now Foundation

name: Creative Growth Art Center
description: Oakland studio for artists with disabilities, whose 12,000-square-foot space includes fiber arts, woodwork, printmaking and ceramics.
details: Gallery, shop (wall art, fashion, jewellery, sculpture) and volunteer opportunities; collaborated on SF Black Art Week 2026.

image.alt: Ceramic houses and sculptures made at Creative Growth Art Center in Oakland
image.credit: Steven Damron from New York / Wikimedia Commons

name: NIAD Art Center
description: Richmond art studio and gallery for artists with disabilities, whose shop includes jewellery and fashion made in the studio.
details: Events and exhibitions open to visitors; volunteer and collaboration options.

image.alt: An artist painting at a table in the NIAD Art Center studio

name: Berkeley Art Center
description: Berkeley community art centre with exhibitions of Bay Area artists and a member directory.
details: Current: 'I see every wave', Sept 12-Nov 22, 2026.

image.alt: The wooden entrance of the Berkeley Art Center in Live Oak Park

name: Rhythmix Cultural Works
description: Alameda arts centre with classes and workshops, the K Gallery and public-art walks.
details: Also home of Maze Daiko taiko; Island City Waterways art walks.

image.alt: A band playing to a full house at Rhythmix Cultural Works

name: Oakland Asian Cultural Center
description: Chinatown cultural centre with weekly art, music and dance classes and exhibitions, a warm entry point into Oakland's Asian American arts community.
details: Suite 290. Accepts exhibition proposals.

image.alt: A hand drawing on paper beside a watercolour palette

name: East Bay Open Studios (Oakland Art Murmur)
description: Self-guided tour of artist studios across Alameda and Contra Costa counties over several weekends, run by Oakland Art Murmur alongside its First Fridays.
details: Art Murmur also runs an Emerging Artist Program and Oakland Style Week. Pin is approximate.

image.alt: Visitors looking at a wall of small artworks in an open studio

name: Art Works Downtown
description: Downtown San Rafael building of artist studios and galleries with a studio residency and a monthly art walk.
details: Studio artist applications and the Max Thelen Studio Residency; galleries 1337 and Founders'. Hosted Tapestry Weavers West shows in the past.

image.alt: The gallery at Art Works Downtown with sculptures on plinths and paintings on the walls

name: MarinMOCA
description: Marin's contemporary art museum, with exhibitions, learning programmes and free family art days.
details: 'In Other Words' curated by Tucker Nichols, Sept 26-Dec 20, 2026. Open Wed-Sun.

image.alt: An artist at work in front of a large plaid painting at Marin MOCA

name: Marin Open Studios
description: Two May weekends when Marin artists open their studios, a natural way to find makers in the county.
details: 2026 dates were May 2-3 and May 9-10. Pin approximate (county-wide).

image.alt: An artist standing in her studio among landscape paintings, Marin Open Studios

name: Pacific Art League
description: Downtown Palo Alto art school and gallery with a full seasonal class catalogue and member exhibitions.
details: Fall 2026 catalogue online.

image.alt: Artists painting and drawing at easels in a Pacific Art League class

name: Silicon Valley Open Studios
description: May open-studios tour across the Peninsula, South Bay and coast, look for the yellow signs.
details: 2026 directory and maps (North, South, Coast) online. Pin approximate (region-wide).

name: Scintillant Studio
description: Mission District jewellery studio teaching eight-week evening semesters for beginners and intermediates, including wax carving and casting.
details: Fall 2026 classes run Mon-Thu evenings 6-9pm (Oct 12-Dec 10); tuition $525 per semester. Winter (Jan-Mar) enrolment opens Nov 1. Studio rentals available. Run by Adam Clark.

image.alt: Hands setting a stone at a jeweller's bench at Scintillant Studio

name: Silverwork Studios (Sausalito)
description: Beginner-friendly guided jewellery sessions where you learn to solder and design your own sterling silver piece, walkable from the San Francisco ferry.
details: Second studio at 1824 Fourth Street, Berkeley. Open Wednesday-Sunday by appointment; sessions of 1-3 hours, holiday workshops.

image.alt: A hand holding a torch and tweezers over a soldering block at Silverwork Studios

name: Renegade Craft Fair San Francisco (Nov 2026)
address: Festival Pavilion, Fort Mason Center, San Francisco, CA 94123
description: Big curated craft fair at Fort Mason's Festival Pavilion, one of 15 Renegade fairs a year; open to apply as a vendor.
details: November 14-15, 2026, Fort Mason Center Festival Pavilion.

image.alt: Banners hung over the crowd at a Renegade Craft Fair in a large hall

name: Alameda Point Antiques Faire
description: Northern California's largest antiques show, 800+ dealers on the first Sunday of every month: vintage textiles, tools and pottery to study and buy.
details: Next: Sunday Nov 1, 2026. Tiered entry: VIP 6-7:30am $20, early buy $15, morning $10, afternoon $5.

image.alt: A folding table of vintage kitchenware at the Alameda Point Antiques Faire

name: Root Division Artist Fair (Dec 2026)
description: Free, all-ages December artist fair at Root Division with an open call for vendors, a low-key first place to sell her work.
details: Saturday Dec 12, 2026, 12-5pm.

image.alt: A visitor looking at framed prints at a Root Division event

name: Maker Faire Bay Area (Mare Island)
description: Three days of robots, fire, fabrication and handmade wonders on Mare Island; returns Sept 24-26, 2027.
details: Call for Makers opens ahead of each faire. Pin approximate (Mare Island).

image.alt: The shark-faced Sharkmobile art car at Maker Faire Bay Area
